messages:
Mira Chen: Quick heads-up — proposal to change attribution for impersonation flows. Today we fully attribute usage to the impersonated service account's project. We're proposing a blended attribution: 80% to the origin project (caller) and 20% to the service-account project.
Sam Nguyen: Why 80/20?
Mira Chen: Practical reasons: billing teams want origin visibility, infra wants SA-level trace. 80/20 keeps incentives aligned while preserving SA-level observability. Open to different split.
Tyler Roberts: This affects quota enforcement too right? If we split, which quota do we decrement?
Mira Chen: Good Q. Proposal: enforce against the origin project's quota primarily, but decrement SA quota counters for the 20% slice so we can detect unusual SA usage. Enforcement priority remains origin -> SA fallback.
Jessica Park: UX question — how do we show this in console billing/usage? Customers will ask why numbers don't sum.
Mira Chen: Console: add a small ‘blended attribution’ table in the usage view showing origin vs SA allocation per request. Also a tooltip explaining rounding and sampling.
Sam Nguyen: Telemetry-wise we should tag every request with both project ids and the attribution weights. Will increase tag cardinality.
Tyler Roberts: Perf + storage cost concern. Can we sample attribution detail at 10%? full counts still go to origin aggregate counters.
Mira Chen: Proposal: full origin counters (low cardinality), sampled SA attribution events (high cardinality) at configurable rate. Default 10% for the canary.
Jessica Park: What about APIs? Will clients need to change headers?
Mira Chen: No required client changes. We'll emit internal header to downstream services for routing: `X-RW-Origin-Project: <proj>` and `X-RW-Impersonated-SA: <sa>` but that's internal only. Public API surface unchanged.
Sam Nguyen: Any authz implications? If a customer pins SA billing to a project, they might see unexpected charges.
Mira Chen: We'll add an admin toggle: org-level control to opt-out of blended attribution. Default on for new orgs during rollout.
Tyler Roberts: Rollout plan? Canary? metrics?
Mira Chen: Canary in prod for 10% of orgs for 2 weeks. Watch metrics: authz-mismatch rate, quota-exhaustion spikes, billing delta (origin vs expected), SA anomaly alerts. If authz-mismatch > 0.5% or quota surprises occur, revert.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: attribution-blend-v1 -> canary ring at 2026-04-05T03:00Z (sha: ad3f9c).
Jessica Park: Console UX work: I'll add a compact card on the usage page and a deeper drilldown for SA-level sampled events. Will need mockups by EOD Tue.
Sam Nguyen: Need a migration note in our API changelog and a short FAQ for billing teams.
Tyler Roberts: Implementation detail — we need to ensure existing rate limiter keys stay the same to avoid changing hot keys. Keep rate-limiter bucketing by origin project only.
Mira Chen: Agreed. Rate limiter: origin project only. SA counters are async and sampled.
Jessica Park: For the telemetry dashboard, suggest a new panel: "Attribution delta" that shows blended vs legacy counts over time.
Sam Nguyen: Also log a debug-level field `attribution_split` for troubleshooting, only for sampled traces.
Mira Chen: Security check: make sure we don't bleed SA cryptographic identities into logs. Use opaque SA IDs.
Tyler Roberts: I'll sketch the dataflow: authn -> attribute weights -> primary quota decrement -> async SA event pipeline (sampled) -> billing/console. Will post to the design doc.
Mira Chen: Thanks — can everyone add +1 or concerns in this thread by EOD? I want to freeze design before we start canary.
Jessica Park: +1 (will post mockups tomorrow).
Sam Nguyen: +1, but want a knob to disable sampled SA events org-wide.
Tyler Roberts: +1, will add rate-limiter note to doc.
ops-bot: Canary started: attribution-blend-v1 -> ring=canary (10%) at 2026-04-05T03:00Z. Monitoring: authz-mismatch: 0.03%, quota-exhaustion: no change.
Mira Chen: Thanks all — tracking follow-ups: mockups (Jessica), design doc edits (Tyler), FAQ & changelog (Sam).
